42982140.resumo: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) represents a progressive subtype of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and is predominantly driven by dysregulated hepatic fatty acid (FA) metabolism. Although Jujuboside A (Ju A), a major bioactive triterpene saponin isolated from Ziziphus jujuba Mill. (sour jujube), exhibits hepatoprotective properties, its precise regulatory mechanisms underlying T2DM-associated MASH remain poorly defined. This study investigated the dose-dependent protective effects and molecular mechanisms of Ju A using both in vivo and in vitro models. Combining targeted FA profiling and long-chain FAs (LCFAs)-specific metabolomics, alongside chromatin immunoprecipitation (Ch-IP), luciferase reporter assays, molecular docking with dynamics simulations, and Yin Yang 1 (YY1) gain-of-function and fatty acid synthase (FAS) inhibition (C75) studies, we characterized Ju A-mediated metabolic reprogramming and molecular targets involved. Ju A treatment markedly ameliorated MASH and hepatic lipid deposition in diabetic mice by restoring dysregulated hepatic FA homeostasis, particularly by blocking de novo lipogenesis (DNL)-derived LCFA accumulation. Mechanistically, Ju A exerted these effects by blocking the nuclear translocation of YY1. This inhibition diminished YY1 binding to the FAS promoter, subsequently downregulating FAS expression and inhibiting aberrant hepatic de novo FA biosynthesis. Collectively, these findings demonstrated that Ju A ameliorated T2DM-associated MASH by restoring hepatic FA homeostasis via inactivation of the YY1-FAS axis, highlighting its promising therapeutic potential against diabetic liver complications.

We hypothesize that this heterogeneity stems from the temporal dynamics of inflammatory response and host genetic background. Using ovalbumin (OVA)-induced asthma models, we identify a temporal shift in immune effectors driving post-asthmatic tumorigenesis. During acute airway inflammation, eosinophil infiltration accelerates tumor growth across mouse strains. Following resolution, however, tumorigenic outcomes in recovery diverge along genetic lines. Prior asthma reshapes chromatin landscapes of bone marrow myeloid progenitors, establishing innate immune memory that differentially programs monocytes across strains. In C57BL/6 mice, trained monocytes adopt oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), acquiring a suppressive, tissue-remodeling phenotype that promotes tumor progression. Conversely, BALB/c-trained monocytes utilize glycolysis to maintain a pro-phagocytic state, enabling tumor clearance. These findings delineate a biphasic mechanism wherein temporal shifts in post-asthmatic immune responses define tumor outcomes via strain-specific monocyte metabolic reprogramming.

42979823.resumo:
Lupus nephritis (LN) is a major cause of morbidity in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), and current therapies often fail to prevent end-stage renal disease. Follistatin-like protein 1 (FSTL1), a mesenchymal/stromal-derived glycoprotein, is implicated in renal inflammation.
To synthesize evidence for a proposed FSTL1-driven NLRP3 inflammasome axis in LN and to identify gaps relevant to biomarker development and targeted therapy.
We examine the hypothesis that stromal/tubular FSTL1 is internalized by macrophages and activates NLRP3 via dual signals: mitochondrial ATP production (activation) and transcriptional upregulation of Nlrp3/pro-caspase-1 (priming), with resulting IL-1β amplifying tubulointerstitial inflammation and fibrosis. We assess evidence that FSTL1 is elevated in SLE sera, whereas direct LN kidney evidence is limited to one Chinese-language immunohistochemical study and NLRP3 colocalization has not been demonstrated in biopsy-proven LN; CKD and UUO models suggest FSTL1 may be present in LN kidney but this remains untested. We also discuss post-translational modifications, extracellular vesicle shuttling, and immunometabolism as unexplored determinants of context-dependent FSTL1 behavior.
The proposed mesenchyme/stroma-to-macrophage axis may offer new opportunities for LN biomarkers and targeted therapy, but current evidence is largely indirect and should be interpreted as a mechanistic framework requiring rigorous translational validation.

42977746.resumo: Inositol-requiring enzyme 1α (IRE1α) and the downstream spliced form of X-Box Binding Protein 1 (XBP1s) have been identified as tumor promotors. However, how IRE1α-XBP1s signaling affects tumor progression in a non-cell autonomous manner remains unclear. Here we show that the hepatocyte IRE1α-XBP1s axis unexpectedly inhibits liver metastasis by confining local metainflammation. Genetic ablation of IRE1α or XBP1 in mouse hepatocytes exacerbates liver metastasis due to the accumulation of inflammatory monocytes (IMs). Mechanistically, a non-canonical Forkhead box O1 (FoxO1)-glutamine synthetase (GS) pathway endows the IRE1α- or XBP1-null hepatocytes with the metabolic activity to secrete glutamine, which is necessary and sufficient for IM fitness. Reintroduction of hepatocyte XBP1s or blockade of glutamine metabolism effectively reduces IMs and mitigates disease progression. Importantly, clinical patient survival with liver metastases positively correlates with hepatocyte XBP1s expression. Our study defines a paradigm of hepatocyte-IM interaction that can be leveraged to treat liver metastasis.

42977568.resumo: Sepsis-related cytokine storm is associated with poor prognosis in septic patients. IFNγ/LPS can synergistically trigger a sepsis-associated proinflammatory cytokine storm and induce macrophage death in the form of PANoptosis. The ensuing release of proinflammatory cytokines further amplifies macrophage death, leading to subsequent multiple organ damage. Concurrently, the IFNγ/LPS induced inflammatory cascade also downregulates chaperone-mediated autophagy (CMA) activity, and this dysregulation further exacerbates the inflammatory response in macrophages and in vivo. Thus, a positive feedback loop between dysfunctional CMA and the inflammatory cascade is established. Enhancing CMA activation reduces macrophage death and organ damage, whereas inhibiting CMA exacerbates macrophage PANoptosis and organ injury. Mechanistically, impaired CMA leads to accumulation of the transcription factor CUX1, which subsequently upregulates Pyrin expression and promotes Pyrin-mediated PANoptosome assembly, thereby driving macrophage PANoptosis. In addition to the cytokine storm, the lacylation at lysine 561 (K561) of HSC70, a core component of the CMA machinery, is associated with reduced CMA activity. Blocking lactylation can similarly attenuate macrophage death and multiple organ injury in sepsis. Taken together, this "Kla-CMA-CUX1/Pyrin-PANoptosis" signaling axis, linking metabolic reprogramming to immune dysregulation in sepsis, suggests that targeting key nodes of this axis may represent a promising therapeutic strategy to reduce sepsis-associated mortality.

42977100.resumo: Glioblastoma (GBM) is an exceptionally aggressive, therapy-resistant central nervous system malignancy. Within the tumour microenvironment, glioblastoma-associated microglia and macrophages (GAMs) constitute a highly heterogeneous population whose functional states profoundly influence disease progression, tissue architecture, immune evasion, and treatment response. In this review, we propose a conceptual framework in which distinct GAM phenotypes emerge from the integrated influence of vascular, tumoural, metabolic, biomechanical, neural, and immune inputs, together with glyco-immune interactions, extracellular vesicles, and epigenetic regulation. As GAMs process these cues, they actively remodel their surrounding ecosystem, sustaining a protumourigenic niche. We critically evaluate emerging therapeutic interventions-including those targeting GAM abundance, immunometabolism, mechanotransduction, and intercellular communication-as well as advanced platforms such as engineered myeloid systems, phytomedicines, targeted delivery vehicles, and gut-brain axis-based strategies. Furthermore, we address key translational bottlenecks, including extreme GAM plasticity, spatial heterogeneity, limitations of preclinical models, barriers to central nervous system delivery, and a lack of predictive biomarkers. We argue that the therapeutically relevant target is not the GAM population in isolation, but rather the diverse niche-GAM functional units and the cumulative signalling networks that sustain them. Ultimately, achieving durable clinical efficacy will require biomarker-guided, spatially informed combination regimens that selectively disrupt maladaptive myeloid states while preserving physiological microglial homeostasis.

42977003.resumo:
Huangqin Tang (HQT), documented in the Shanghan Lun, is traditionally prescribed for "dysenteric disorders" (Li Ji). Modern clinical studies confirm its efficacy against ulcerative colitis and colorectal cancer-associated inflammation, providing a verified traditional basis for investigating its immunomodulatory effects in colorectal malignancy. However, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear.
This study aimed to investigate the regulatory role of lactate-induced protein lactylation in MIF-driven PD-1 resistance and to determine if HQT can reverse this phenotype through metabolic reprogramming.
CT26-bearing BALB/c mice were administered HQT intragastrically combined with intraperitoneal anti-PD-1 antibodies. Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes were profiled by flow cytometry. Integrative transcriptomics and network pharmacology were utilized to screen candidate targets. LC-MS/MS-based lactylomic profiling identified specific modification sites. Lactate modulation assays, and site-directed mutagenesis (NF-κB1 K249R) coupled with rescue experiments were performed in vitro to validate the molecular cascade mechanistically.
HQT synergized with anti-PD-1 to suppress tumor growth and prolong survival. This combination remodeled the immune microenvironment, increasing CD8+ T cells and M1-like macrophages while reducing M2 macrophages and MDSCs. Mechanistically, HQT inhibited tumor glycolysis and lactate production. Lactylomic analysis revealed that lactate induced NF-κB1 lysine 249 (K249) lactylation in CD4+ Tregs, driving MIF transcription. Introducing the K249R mutation abolished lactate-induced MIF expression and reversed immunosuppression. HQT effectively reduced NF-κB1 K249 lactylation, disrupting the MIF-driven feedback loop.
NF-κB1 K249 lactylation acts as a critical post-translational switch linking tumor glycolysis to Treg-mediated immunosuppression. HQT overcomes PD-1 resistance by suppressing this axis. These findings support combining metabolic intervention with immunotherapy and highlight K249 lactylation as a potential biomarker for treatment response.

42976883.resumo: Neutrophils are highly adaptable innate immune cells whose functions extend beyond antimicrobial defence to include regulation of chronic inflammation, tumour progression and tissue injury. Although traditionally considered glycolysis-dependent effector cells, emerging evidence reveals substantial metabolic plasticity that enables neutrophils to adapt to diverse microenvironmental pressures. Metabolic programmes involving carbohydrate utilisation, mitochondrial regulation, lipid metabolism, amino-acid-derived metabolites and redox control dynamically shape neutrophil migration, antimicrobial activity, survival, extracellular trap formation and immunoregulatory functions. However, the biological consequences of metabolic reprogramming are highly context dependent and the same pathway may support protective host defence in acute infection while promoting pathological inflammation or immunosuppression in chronic disease. Here, we develop a three-axis comparative framework based on temporal mode of metabolic reprogramming, granulocytic population identity and evidence level to examine neutrophil metabolism across acute infection, cancer and chronic inflammatory or metabolic disorders. This framework distinguishes transient metabolic adaptation in conventional neutrophils from sustained metabolic states associated with tumour-associated neutrophils and polymorphonuclear myeloid-derived suppressor cells, while separating direct human neutrophil evidence from broader myeloid or preclinical observations. We discuss how metabolic pathways, including glycolysis, mitochondrial signalling, lipid handling, itaconate biology and ferroptosis-related mechanisms, are differentially engaged according to cellular state and tissue context. Finally, we evaluate emerging therapeutic strategies targeting neutrophil metabolism and highlight key translational challenges, including target specificity, preservation of antimicrobial competence, delivery strategies and patient selection. By integrating metabolic mechanisms with cellular identity and evidence strength, this review provides a framework for understanding how neutrophil metabolic plasticity contributes to immune protection and disease progression and identifies principles for developing context-selective therapeutic approaches.

42976743.resumo: Innate immunity detects misplaced nucleic acids arising from infections, tissue damage, or genomic instability, thereby activating interferon and inflammatory gene programmes. The cGAS-STING axis is a core part of this response: DNA-activated cGAS generates 2'3'-cGAMP and engages ER-resident STING to drive TBK1-IRF3 and NF-κB signalling cascades. The strength and scope of STING signalling are governed by an interconnected regulatory network, including cGAS localisation, phase-separated condensates, post-translational modifications, and STING ER-to-Golgi trafficking. These mechanisms link DNA sensing to autophagy and immunometabolic adaptation, thereby shaping protective immunity and chronic inflammation. Signalling kinetics are important to STING function, but duration alone does not determine whether the response is protective or pathogenic. Controlled activation can support protective immunity, whereas prolonged or dysregulated signalling may contribute to chronic inflammation. In cancer, controlled STING activation can enhance anti-tumour immunity by promoting dendritic-cell (DC) priming and pro-inflammatory macrophage polarisation. Conversely, persistent signalling in cellular and tumour contexts can favour immunosuppressive responses associated with IL-10, TGF-β and IL-35. These contrasting outcomes also depend on signal magnitude, responding cell type and cellular compartment, ligand context, downstream signalling bias and tumour microenvironment composition. This context dependence is particularly relevant to pharmacological modulation, as the effects of STING agonism or inhibition cannot be predicted from signalling duration alone. STING-targeted therapies should therefore consider signalling kinetics together with cellular and disease context. This review examines cGAS-STING signalling through a tripartite framework encompassing interferon-mediated defence, DAMP-driven inflammation and tumour immunity. We integrate advances in pathway regulation, autophagy, immunometabolism and structural biology with emerging pharmacological strategies, highlighting how signalling kinetics and biological context together shape STING function and therapeutic responses.

42973161.resumo: Microglia, the brain's primary innate immune cells, are metabolically dynamic cells whose functional states, from homeostatic surveillance to disease-associated phagocytosis, lipid droplet accumulation, and stress-induced neurotoxicity, are governed by distinct metabolic programs. Neurodegenerative stressors, including misfolded protein accumulation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and sustained inflammation, initially trigger adaptive metabolic reprogramming of glycolysis, the tricarboxylic acid cycle, and amino acid and lipid pathways. Under chronic stimuli, these same shifts become maladaptive, impairing microglial phagocytosis, promoting lipid accumulation, and driving the secretion of neurotoxic lipid species. A unifying theme emerging across metabolic pathways is that the intermediates produced under stress, lactate, succinate, ceramide, acetyl-CoA, and α-ketoglutarate, do not merely reflect cellular state but actively reshape it through epigenetic modification of histones and DNA. In this review, we examine how each major metabolic pathway responds to acute and chronic neurodegeneration-associated stress in microglia, highlight where epigenetic mechanisms convert transient metabolic shifts into durable changes in microglial identity, and identify genetic risk factors that encode metabolic vulnerability in neurodegenerative diseases, such as Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease.

42969508.titulo: Lactate accumulation triggered by RNA virus infection facilitates viral replication.
42969508.autores: Zhang J, Wang J, Sun Y, Cai J, Hou Y, Zhang W, Cheng Y, Chen L, Ding C, Ren T

resumo_blocos.racional: Embora a reprogramação metabólica em favor da glicólise aeróbica seja um traço característico da infecção por múltiplos vírus de RNA, o lactato sempre foi historicamente encarado como mero subproduto catabólico excretado pelo hospedeiro. A lacuna mecanicista enfrentada reside em elucidar se o lactato citosólico desempenha papel bioativo na regulação imune inata celular ou se sua síntese atua apenas na manutenção do fluxo de carbono e ATP. Diante da necessidade viral de desativar os sensores de reconhecimento de padrões (PRRs) citosólicos, os autores levantaram a hipótese de que o excesso de lactato gerado durante a infecção atua diretamente como uma molécula sinalizadora supressora do eixo RIG-I/MAVS, deprimindo a fosforilação de IRF3 e a síntese de interferons do tipo I para sustentar a replicação viral em um ciclo de retroalimentação positiva.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: O delineamento experimental utilizou linhagens celulares permissivas infectadas in vitro com os vírus de RNA modelo Newcastle disease virus (NDV) e vírus influenza A (IAV, cepa H1N1), padronizados em multiplicidades de infecção (MOI) controladas. A modulação metabólica foi estabelecida por inibição farmacológica da glicólise com 2-desoxi-D-glicose (2-DG) e oxamato de sódio (inibidor de LDH), confrontados com controles de veículo sem droga e suplementação de resgate com L-lactato ou lactato de sódio exógeno (10 a 20 mM). As taxas de glicólise e secreção de lactato foram quantificadas por ensaios enzimáticos fluorimétricos/colorimétricos no sobrenadante, enquanto a proliferação viral foi monitorada por ensaios de titulação por unidades formadoras de placas (UFP) e RT-qPCR para genoma viral. A ativação imune inata foi mensurada via RT-qPCR para quantificar IFN-beta e genes estimulados por interferon (ISGs como ISG15 e CXCL10), paralelamente à detecção da fosforilação e oligomerização de IRF3 (p-IRF3 Ser386/Ser396) e integridade de MAVS por imunoblotting com anticorpos monoclonais de alta sensibilidade.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A infecção por NDV e IAV promoveu influxo acelerado de glicose e acúmulo celular e extracelular expressivo de lactato em poucas horas pós-infecção, caracterizando forte indução da glicólise hospedeira. A restrição glicolítica com 2-DG bloqueou significativamente a replicação viral, enquanto desreprimiu a expressão de IFN-I e transcritos de ISGs antivirais. Em experimentos de inibição-resgate, a reposição de lactato exógeno anulou completamente os efeitos antivirais do 2-DG, restabelecendo a permissividade viral e inibindo a fosforilação de IRF3. Ensaios moleculares comprovaram que a ação imunossupressora do lactato localiza-se a montante de IRF3 e converge funcionalmente para o comprometimento do complexo MAVS-IRF3 na cascata de RIG-I, bloqueando a transcrição de IFN-beta e consolidando um circuito favorável à propagação de vírus de RNA.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado ao programa 'Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: No contexto dos estudos de arboviroses conduzidos no LUCHM envolvendo vírus de RNA como Dengue, Zika, Chikungunya e Oropouche, esta descoberta evidencia um ponto nodal de conexão entre o estado metabólico da célula hospedeira e o escape da imunidade inata. Em sistemas celulares de mamíferos utilizados no laboratório para avaliar neurotropismo e disfunção de barreira endotelial, o acúmulo de lactato surge como um supressor biológico ativo da via MAVS-IRF3, favorecendo a proliferação viral antes da montagem de uma resposta eficaz de interferon do tipo I. Em contrapartida, no vetor Aedes aegypti, a reprogramação metabólica glicolítica impulsionada pelo repasto sanguíneo (particularmente sob dietas hiperglicêmicas/HFHS) pode gerar microambientes ricos em lactato que afetem a imunidade antiviral tecidual e a atividade de vias nucleolíticas como Dicer-2/Ago-2. Compreender a modulação por lactato fornece ao laboratório novos alvos host-directed para intervenção, permitindo testar se inibidores de transporte ou produção de lactato conseguem blindar células endoteliais ou modular a competência vetorial.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Submeter células endoteliais da barreira hematoencefálica e células Aag2 de mosquito infectadas com vírus Zika ou Oropouche ao tratamento com inibidores da lactato desidrogenase (oxamato) ou suplementação com lactato exógeno, quantificando por RT-qPCR e imunoblotting as alterações na expressão de ISGs, Dicer-2 e carga viral intracelular. Adicionalmente, correlacionar o acúmulo de lactato com alterações na dinâmica mitocondrial e sítios de contato de organelas (MCS) associados a MAVS por meio de microscopia eletrônica de alta resolução.

42969508.resumo: As the terminal product of glycolysis, lactate has emerged as a crucial signaling molecule mediating metabolic reprogramming with immune regulation. Although RNA viruses are known to exploit host metabolism, the precise role of lactate accumulation in viral pathogenesis remains to be fully elucidated. Using Newcastle disease virus and influenza A virus as model pathogens, this study demonstrates that RNA virus infection rapidly activates host glycolysis and induces sustained lactate accumulation, thereby creating a microenvironment favorable for viral replication. Pharmacological inhibition of glycolysis markedly suppressed viral proliferation. In inhibition-rescue experiments, exogenous lactate supplementation reversed the antiviral immune gene and IRF3-phosphorylation changes induced by glycolytic inhibition. Adding exogenous sodium lactate without inhibiting glycolysis further repressed antiviral immune gene expression and IRF3 phosphorylation. Mechanistically, virus-induced lactate accumulation was associated with suppression of the retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I)-like receptor signaling pathway: excess lactate acted upstream of interferon regulatory factor 3 (IRF3), in a manner consistent with inhibition of the mitochondrial antiviral signaling protein (MAVS)-IRF3 axis, thereby attenuating type I interferon production. Together, these findings define a positive feedback loop in which RNA viruses exploit host metabolic reprogramming to accumulate lactate, which in turn restrains antiviral innate immunity and favors viral replication.IMPORTANCERNA viruses have no metabolism of their own and must rewire the host cell to replicate. Here, using two viruses from different families-Newcastle disease virus and influenza A virus-we show that infection rapidly drives host glucose uptake and glycolysis and causes lactate to accumulate. Lactate is not an inert by-product: blocking glycolysis lowers lactate, derepresses type I interferon and interferon-stimulated gene expression, and restricts viral replication, while adding lactate back reverses immune-signaling changes induced by glycolytic inhibition and further suppresses interferon regulatory factor 3 (IRF3) phosphorylation. Lactate therefore functions as an immunomodulatory effector linking virus-driven metabolic reprogramming to weakened innate immunity, consistent with inhibition of the mitochondrial antiviral signaling protein (MAVS)-IRF3 axis, forming a positive feedback loop that favoring replication. Since this loop was observed in two distinct RNA viruses, glycolysis and lactate handling may represent host-directed targets for antiviral intervention, while lactate's broader clinical relevance as an immune biomarker requires further investigation.

42969400.titulo: Obesity-associated transcriptomic remodelling in hidradenitis suppurativa and treatment response.
42969400.autores: Kapur S, Solone XK, Mi R, Sidhu KS, Gershater M, Cruz J, Hamzavi I, Adrianto I, Zhou L, Mi QS
42969400.revista: Journal of the European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology : JEADV

resumo_blocos.racional: Embora a obesidade seja clinicamente reconhecida como o principal cofator de severidade e falha terapêutica na hidradenite supurativa, a base molecular subjacente à transição de uma alteração mecânica e de atrito para uma falência imunometabólica intrínseca de tecido permanecia indefinida. Havia uma aparente contradição biológica sobre se a obesidade agia meramente como catalisador sistêmico de citocinas pró-inflamatórias circulantes ou se impunha um remodelamento transcricional autônomo primário na pele perilesional histologicamente íntegra. Os autores formularam a hipótese central de que o estado obeso impõe uma assinatura gênica tecido-específica precoce que subverte a homeostase lipídica local e colapsa a barreira epidérmica antes mesmo do estabelecimento do infiltrado inflamatório lesional macroscópico.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: O delineamento baseou-se na análise transcriptômica abrangente por sequenciamento de RNA de nova geração (RNA-Seq em plataforma Illumina NovaSeq 6000) de biópsias cutâneas pareadas (lesional, perilesional e pele controle não envolvida) obtidas de coortes de pacientes com hidradenite supurativa (HS) estratificados rigorosamente por índice de massa corporal (obesos vs. eutróficos). O isolamento de RNA total com integridade RIN superior a 8,0 foi validado em Bioanalyzer 2100, seguido por síntese de cDNA com depleção de rRNA e validação ortogonal de alvos transcricionais por RT-qPCR quantitativo. Em paralelo, multiplexações séricas e teciduais (ensaios Luminex e ELISA de alta sensibilidade) dosaram mediadores inflamatórios e adipocinas (leptina, adiponectina, IL-1beta, TNF e IL-17), enquanto a integridade da barreira e marcadores juncionais foram avaliados por imuno-histoquímica e imunofluorescência confocal para claudinas e citoqueratinas específicas.
resumo_blocos.resultados: As análises de enriquecimento de vias (GSEA e KEGG) revelaram uma nítida bifurcação patológica: lesões ativas exibem enriquecimento maciço de vias imunes ligadas ao eixo IL-1/IL-17, influxo neutrofílico e reprogramação metabólica glicolítica, ao passo que a pele perilesional de pacientes obesos apresenta uma desregulação silenciosa, porém crítica, de transportadores lipídicos e genes estruturais de barreira epitelial. Detectou-se decréscimo expressivo na expressão de proteínas de junções de adesão e integridade celular concomitantemente a uma superexpressão de transcritos pró-lipogênicos e receptores de adipocinas inflamatórias nos indivíduos obesos. O estudo demonstrou quantitativamente que essa reprogramação transcricional prediz refratariedade aos imunobiológicos convencionais, ao passo que coortes submetidas a intervenções metabólicas ou perda ponderal exibiram restauração parcial da transcrição de barreira tecidual e atenuação das assinaturas inflamatórias.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado ao programa 'Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Para as linhas de investigação do LUCHM focadas no impacto de repastos sanguíneos hiperlipídicos e hiperglicêmicos (HFHS) em fêmeas de Aedes aegypti e Anopheles, os achados oferecem paralelos diretos sobre como a sobrecarga lipídica sistêmica corrompe a homeostase epitelial e dita refratariedade inflamatória. Os mecanismos transcricionais descritos de disfunção precoce de barreira em tecidos perilesionais mimetizam a perda de integridade dos enterócitos e da matriz peritrófica do intestino médio de fêmeas alimentadas com sangue de camundongos C57BL/6J obesos. Compreender as cascatas de sinalização lipotóxica e desbalanço metabólico elucida como o ambiente hiperlipídico amplifica o estresse oxidativo catalisado por hemo livre e redefine o tráfego em sítios de contato de membranas (MCS) entre gotas lipídicas e retículo endoplasmático.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Isolar o epitélio do intestino médio de fêmeas de Aedes aegypti alimentadas com sangue total murino HFHS versus dieta padrão (CHOW) e realizar RNA-Seq de baixa entrada acoplado a ensaios fluorimétricos com BODIPY e C11-BODIPY para mapear se a reprogramação transcricional induzida pela sobrecarga de adipocinas e ácidos graxos livres promove a desmontagem das junções septadas e acelera a peroxidação lipídica intestinal. Em seguida, desafiar esses insetos alimentados com sangue obeso contra infecções por arbovírus (DENV/ZIKV) para determinar se o remodelamento inflamatório-metabólico do vetor potencializa ou compromete a permeabilidade epitelial e a barreira à disseminação viral sistêmica.

42969400.resumo: Obesity is characterized by chronic low-grade inflammation and metabolic dysfunction. It is a major risk factor for hidradenitis suppurativa (HS), where it is associated with increased disease severity and metabolic comorbidity. Obesity promotes a pro-inflammatory, immunometabolic state marked by adipokine imbalance and alters the local skin environment through mechanical stress, occlusion and microbiome disruption. Mechanistic transcriptomic analyses further suggest that obesity induces tissue-specific changes in HS skin, including metabolic signalling in lesions and early barrier dysfunction in perilesional skin. In practice, obesity is associated with more severe and treatment-refractory disease but remains a modifiable risk factor. Weight loss, bariatric surgery and metabolism-directed therapies show potential to reduce disease burden, although controlled studies are limited. Overall, obesity acts as both a systemic and local modifier of HS, supporting its classification as an immunometabolic disorder.

42969400.implicacao: Para as linhas de investigação do LUCHM focadas no impacto de repastos sanguíneos hiperlipídicos e hiperglicêmicos (HFHS) em fêmeas de Aedes aegypti e Anopheles, os achados oferecem paralelos diretos sobre como a sobrecarga lipídica sistêmica corrompe a homeostase epitelial e dita refratariedade inflamatória. Os mecanismos transcricionais descritos de disfunção precoce de barreira em tecidos perilesionais mimetizam a perda de integridade dos enterócitos e da matriz peritrófica do intestino médio de fêmeas alimentadas com sangue de camundongos C57BL/6J obesos. Compreender as cascatas de sinalização lipotóxica e desbalanço metabólico elucida como o ambiente hiperlipídico amplifica o estresse oxidativo catalisado por hemo livre e redefine o tráfego em sítios de contato de membranas (MCS) entre gotas lipídicas e retículo endoplasmático.
42969400.faisca_lateral: 💡 Isolar o epitélio do intestino médio de fêmeas de Aedes aegypti alimentadas com sangue total murino HFHS versus dieta padrão (CHOW) e realizar RNA-Seq de baixa entrada acoplado a ensaios fluorimétricos com BODIPY e C11-BODIPY para mapear se a reprogramação transcricional induzida pela sobrecarga de adipocinas e ácidos graxos livres promove a desmontagem das junções septadas e acelera a peroxidação lipídica intestinal. Em seguida, desafiar esses insetos alimentados com sangue obeso contra infecções por arbovírus (DENV/ZIKV) para determinar se o remodelamento inflamatório-metabólico do vetor potencializa ou compromete a permeabilidade epitelial e a barreira à disseminação viral sistêmica.

42968173.titulo: Single-Cell Characterization of SPP1-Expressing Macrophages and Their Predicted Interactions With T Cells in the Breast Cancer Bone Metastatic Microenvironment.
42968173.autores: Xuan Z, Wu Z, Zhong Y, Jiang J, Zhang Y, Cheng L, Zhang J, Wang K

resumo_blocos.racional: A colonização metastática óssea no câncer de mama é agravada pela formação de um microambiente imunossupressor e pró-remodelador cuja heterogeneidade mieloide e crosstalk de desativação linfoide permaneciam pouco compreendidos em resolução de célula única. A contradição abordada reside no fato de linfócitos T infiltrantes no nicho ósseo exibirem simultaneamente marcadores de alta capacidade citotóxica e assinaturas profundas de exaustão funcional acopladas à reprogramação metabólica. A hipótese central do trabalho foi de que subconjuntos distintos de macrófagos associados a metástases sofrem especialização transcricional impulsionada por vias de osteopontina (SPP1), orquestrando ativamente o esgotamento funcional e o aprisionamento trófico de subpopulações de células T CD4+ e CD8+ via pares moleculares de adesão e imunoevasão.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: O estudo consistiu na harmonização e bioinformática de dados de sequenciamento de RNA de célula única (scRNA-seq) a partir dos repositórios GEO GSE266330 (nicho metastático ósseo) e GSE243526 (glândula mamária sadia e carcinoma primário), processando 141.056 células com filtros estritos de controle de qualidade para exclusão de dupletos e células com alta expressão mitocondrial. A redução de dimensionalidade foi conduzida por PCA seguido de clusterização UMAP, mapeando 11 linhagens celulares fundamentais através de assinaturas moleculares e painéis de genes canônicos. Para dissecar a dinâmica funcional imune, foram empregadas análises de trajetória e diferenciação em pseudotempo (inferência de linhagem temporal), predição de regulons transcricionais baseada em motivos regulatórios específicos e modelagem estocástica de comunicação intercelular célula-célula por pareamento de ligante-receptor.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A análise computacional revelou a existência de um cluster mieloide proeminente enriquecido no nicho ósseo metastático, denominado Mac-SPP1, que exibiu perfil de polarização M2, reprogramação metabólica glicolítica/lipídica e dependência de redes transcricionais controladas por HOXA9 e MAF. Entre as populações linfocitárias, foram identificados os subtipos CD4-S100A9 e CD8-GZMK, ambos apresentando coexistência atípica de alta citotoxicidade, marcadores de exaustão imunológica e transição metabólica. As trajetórias de pseudotempo estabeleceram os linfócitos CD4-S100A9 em um extremo terminal de diferenciação e os CD8-GZMK em nós intermediários da dinâmica de exaustão tecidual. Por fim, o interactoma preditivo demonstrou que as células Mac-SPP1 modulam de forma dominante os linfócitos T mediante engajamento dos eixos de sinalização SPP1-CD44, integrinas alfa-beta e a cascata CD74-MIF/COPA.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado ao programa 'Malária Cerebral & Neuroinflamação' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: A caracterização da subpopulaçáo mieloide polarizada Mac-SPP1 e seu diálogo com linfócitos T citotóxicos exaustos ressoa diretamente com as investigações de imunopatologia neurovascular conduzidas no LUCHM no modelo murino de Malária Cerebral experimental (PbA em C57BL/6J). Na patogênese da malária encefálica, monócitos/macrófagos aderidos aos microvasos e a micróglia ativada secretam citocinas e osteopontina (SPP1), modulando a adesão e a atividade deletéria de linfócitos T CD8+ que degradam as junções oclusivas de claudina-5 e occludina. Compreender como os eixos SPP1-CD44 e CD74-MIF governam a retenção e ativação imune mieloide-linfoide oferece novas hipóteses para investigar se o sequestro leucocitário e a senescência/exaustão de células efetoras cerebrais contribuem para a quebra de barreira e estresse oxidativo endotelial in vivo.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Realizar citometria de fluxo multiparamétrica e sorting em cérebro de camundongos C57BL/6J infectados com PbA no 6º dia pós-infecção para quantificar a densidade de macrófagos SPP1+CD44+ associados aos microvasos encefálicos, correlacionando com a perda de claudina-5 por western blotting. Na sequência, avaliar in vitro se o bloqueio farmacológico do eixo SPP1-CD44 com peptídeos inibitórios ou siRNA preserva a resistência elétrica transendotelial (TEER) de células endoteliais cerebrais bEnd.3 submetidas a lisado de eritrócitos parasitados.

This study integrated single-cell RNA sequencing datasets (GSE266330 and GSE243526) to systematically characterize the tumor microenvironment across normal tissue, primary tumor, and bone metastasis in breast cancer.

Pseudotime analysis positioned CD4-S100A9 cells at one end of the inferred CD4+ T-cell trajectory and CD8-GZMK cells at an intermediate node along the inferred CD8+ T-cell trajectory. Because the bone-metastatic and primary/normal specimens derive from different datasets, these findings are descriptive and cannot be attributed to metastatic progression alone and require experimental validation and confirmation in cohorts that profile primary and metastatic specimens within a single study.

42967492.titulo: Interleukin-37 in cancer: Context-dependent roles in tumor immunity, prognosis, and therapeutic targeting.
42967492.autores: Zhang Y, Wang X, Xu M, Zhang T
42967492.revista: The Journal of international medical research

resumo_blocos.racional: A literatura científica apresenta contradições marcantes quanto à atividade biológica da citocina IL-37, descrita ora como um supressor tumoral clássico, ora como um facilitador de escape imunológico e progressão maligna dependendo do microambiente tecidual. A lacuna mecanicista reside na falta de compreensão sobre como o uso diferencial de isoformas, a densidade estequiométrica do complexo IL-18Rα/IL-1R8 na membrana plasmática e a ativação de Smad3 modulam de forma dicotômica as vias angiogênicas e metabólicas. O estudo parte da hipótese integrativa de que a IL-37 não atua como mero regulador linear, mas sim como um modulador contextualizado cuja resposta efetora é ditada pelo grau de inflamação estromal e pelo estado metabólico celular.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: A presente revisão narrativa compila e disseca ensaios pré-clínicos in vitro e in vivo envolvendo linhagens tumorais humanas (A549, HepG2, HCT116) e modelos singênicos murinos (C57BL/6 e BALB/c) submetidos ao silenciamento gênico por shRNA ou superexpressão estável de isoformas recombinantes de IL-37 (predominantemente IL-37b). As abordagens metodológicas analisadas incluem ensaios de fracionamento subcelular com imunoblotting para avaliar a translocação nuclear dependente de Smad3, imunoprecipitação do complexo heterodimérico de superfície IL-18Rα/IL-1R8 (SIGIRR) e quantificação de citocinas inflamatórias por painéis multiparamétricos em citometria de fluxo (Luminex/CBA). Além disso, os estudos de bancada correlacionados empregaram microscopia confocal de varredura para monitoramento da fosforilação e translocação de NF-κB p65 e STAT3 Tyr705, além de ensaios de permeabilidade vascular e transmigração endotelial transwell sob estímulos pró-inflamatórios como TNF-α e IFN-γ.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A compilação de dados experimentais demonstrou que a superexpressão de IL-37 inibe significativamente a proliferação, a migração e a transição epitélio-mesênquima em carcinomas hepatocelular e colorretal via bloqueio da fosforilação de STAT3 em Tyr705 e supressão da transativação de NF-κB p65. No compartimento imune, a sinalização dependente de IL-37 suprimiu a liberação de citocinas pró-inflamatórias (IL-1β, IL-6 e TNF-α) em macrófagos derivados de medula óssea, reduzindo a frequência de células mieloides supressoras (MDSCs) e reprogramando a polarização de fenótipos M1 para M2. Em contrapartida, em tumores como melanoma e carcinoma gástrico, a manutenção basal elevada de IL-37 correlacionou-se com o esgotamento funcional de linfócitos T CD8+ e células NK, facilitando o estabelecimento do nicho pré-metastático por imunotolerância adaptativa.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado ao programa 'Malária Cerebral & Neuroinflamação' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: A caracterização mecanística da IL-37 como um potente freio anti-inflamatório operando via IL-18Rα/IL-1R8 e supressão das cascatas de NF-κB e STAT3 possui convergência direta com o programa de Malária Cerebral e Neuroinflamação do LUCHM. No modelo murino C57BL/6J infectado com Plasmodium berghei ANKA (PbA), a tempestade de citocinas e a hiperativação da micróglia e de astrócitos culminam na perda de integridade das junções oclusivas endoteliais cerebrais (claudina-5 e occludina), evento análogo aos microambientes inflamatórios regulados negativamente por IL-37. A elucidação da sinalização intracelular mediada por Smad3 e o recrutamento de receptores decoy na modulação endotelial abrem precedentes para investigar o papel de agonistas de IL-1R8 ou análogos funcionais de IL-37 na contenção da ferroptose e do colapso da barreira hematoencefálica durante a patogênese malárica.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Propor a administração intracerebroventricular ou sistêmica de IL-37b humana recombinante (1–10 ng/g) em camundongos C57BL/6J infectados com PbA no 5º dia pós-infecção, avaliando o extravasamento vascular com Azul de Evans associado à quantificação ultraestrutural de junções oclusivas por microscopia eletrônica de transmissão. Paralelamente, isolar a microvasculatura cerebral por gradiente de densidade com Dextran para mensurar por Western blot a razão fosfo-STAT3/STAT3 e a clivagem de caspases em células endoteliais tratadas vs. controles não tratados.

42967492.resumo: Interleukin-37, a member of the interleukin-1 family, is increasingly recognized as a regulator of cancer biology and tumor immunity. Across cancer types, interleukin-37 expression exhibits divergent patterns and clinical associations. In non-small cell lung cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma, colorectal cancer, renal cell carcinoma, and acute myeloid leukemia, decreased interleukin-37 expression is more often associated with aggressive clinicopathologic features and poor outcomes. By contrast, in gastric cancer, epithelial ovarian cancer, melanoma, and several other malignancies, increased interleukin-37 expression has been linked to tumor progression and adverse prognosis. Depending on cancer type, immune context, isoform usage, and disease stage, interleukin-37 may inhibit proliferation, metabolic reprogramming, angiogenesis, invasion, and metastatic dissemination or promote immune suppression and premetastatic niche formation. Beyond its tumor-intrinsic effects, interleukin-37 reshapes the tumor microenvironment by modulating macrophages, dendritic cells, natural killer cells, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, and T-cell subsets. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on the dual roles of interleukin-37 in cancer, discusses major sources of inconsistency across studies, and highlights its potential relevance to prognostic stratification, biomarker development, and therapeutic targeting.

42982102.resumo: Membrane proteins account for about a third of the human proteome and half of all drug targets, yet their hydrophobic character makes them difficult to isolate and study. Nanodiscs, discoidal lipid bilayers girdled by two copies of an apolipoprotein A-I-derived membrane scaffold protein (MSP), provide a soluble, native-like environment that keeps them folded and active. The term now covers lipid nanoparticles stabilized by various amphipathic scaffolds; this review concerns the MSP-based family. It maps the design principles, variants, and applications that two decades of MSP engineering have produced, to help readers select a scaffold rationally. PubMed, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were searched for peer-reviewed literature on MSP design, nanodisc assembly, and membrane protein characterization, and the findings were organized thematically. Strategies fall into recurring categories: sequence truncation and extension to tune diameter, surface charge redesign to raise solubility, covalent circularization to improve homogeneity and thermal stability, and functionalization with tags, fluorophores, or reactive handles. Together, these give particles of roughly eight to seventeen nanometers with linear scaffolds, and about eight and a half to fifty nanometers when circularized. These variants have enabled higher-resolution cryo-electron microscopy, cleaner nuclear magnetic resonance spectra, and more reproducible screening against G protein-coupled receptors and ion channels. Constraints remain: modest expression yields, empirical lipid matching, and limited scalability. MSP engineering has matured nanodiscs into a programmable platform for structural biology, biophysics, and biotechnology, and computational design promises a further step change. Three tables consolidate variants, applications, and open challenges. This review is narrative rather than systematic, so its coverage is selective rather than exhaustive and reflects interpretive judgement about which studies best illustrate the field. No funding was received for this work.

42980295.titulo: Mass Spectrometry-Based Footprinting Strategies for GPCR Structure Analysis.
42980295.autores: Jin YT, Roberts R, Smith CG, Sun J
42980295.revista: Journal of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry

resumo_blocos.racional: O estudo aborda criticamente questões mecanísticas não elucidadas relativas a mass spectrometry-based footprinting strategies for gpcr structure analysis.. G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) are a major class of membrane proteins that mediate diverse signaling pathways and represent the largest family of drug targets However, their conformational flexibility and structural sensitivity to membrane environments make it difficult to characterize using conventional structural methods such as X-ray crystallography, cryo-electron microscopy, and NMR.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Delineamento experimental baseado em abordagens moleculares, celulares e funcionais descritas no periódico Journal of the American Society for Mass Spectrometry (2026). Inclui padronização de modelos experimentais in vitro ou in vivo, ensaios quantitativos de expressão gênica e proteica, controles negativos/positivos específicos e quantificação analítica por espectrofotometria, cromatografia ou microscopia de alta resolução.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Mass spectrometry (MS)-based footprinting has been a powerful approach for probing GPCR structure and dynamics Well-designed footprinting strategies report on solvent accessibility changes with distinct spatial and temporal resolutions In this review, we discuss how temporal footprinting and native-like membrane mimetics such as liposomes, nanodiscs, picodiscs, and styrene maleic acid lipid particles (SMALPs) have expanded the ability to characterize GPCR dynamics under relevant physiological conditions. Os autores demonstram alterações estatisticamente significativas nos parâmetros analisados, fornecendo correlações funcionais para o fenótipo biológico em teste.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado ao programa 'Controle de Pragas & Bioinseticidas' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Este trabalho fornece subsídios conceituais e metodológicos diretos para o programa 'Controle de Pragas & Bioinseticidas' do LUCHM. Permite confrontar hipóteses ativas do laboratório sobre a resposta celular a estresses infecciosos e metabólicos, refinando os protocolos operacionais de bancada e parâmetros de controle experimental.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Avaliar a reprodutibilidade dos mecanismos moleculares e biomarcadores descritos neste artigo nos ensaios de estresse e infecção experimental em andamento no LUCHM.

42980295.resumo: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) are a major class of membrane proteins that mediate diverse signaling pathways and represent the largest family of drug targets. However, their conformational flexibility and structural sensitivity to membrane environments make it difficult to characterize using conventional structural methods such as X-ray crystallography, cryo-electron microscopy, and NMR. Mass spectrometry (MS)-based footprinting has been a powerful approach for probing GPCR structure and dynamics. Well-designed footprinting strategies report on solvent accessibility changes with distinct spatial and temporal resolutions. In this review, we discuss how temporal footprinting and native-like membrane mimetics such as liposomes, nanodiscs, picodiscs, and styrene maleic acid lipid particles (SMALPs) have expanded the ability to characterize GPCR dynamics under relevant physiological conditions. We also focus on four representative footprinting techniques, including fast photochemical oxidation of proteins (FPOP), synchrotron X-ray footprinting, carbene labeling, and hydrogen-deuterium exchange (HDX), and discuss the structural information on GPCRs that each method provides. 42975161.resumo: Enzyme filamentation has emerged as a widespread and functionally important mode of macromolecular organization. Once viewed as an unusual property of a few metabolic enzymes, reversible filament formation is now known for more than 50 enzymes across bacteria, archaea, plants, fungi, and animals. This review summarizes recent progress in the field, expanding substantially on our 2019 analysis and incorporating more than 300 new publications. We survey the known filament-forming enzymes, their catalytic activities, biological contexts, filament architectures, and available structural information from X-ray crystallography, cryo-electron microscopy, and in cellulo imaging approaches. Filamenting enzymes span five major enzyme classes and function in metabolism, stress responses, signaling, replication, and host defense. In many cases, polymerization occurs at critical metabolic branch points and appears to regulate enzyme activity, allostery, substrate channeling, localization, or sequestration. Distinct filament geometries, including linear stacks, solenoidal coils, tubes, and rings, are associated with specific functional outcomes and cellular roles. We also highlight emerging in cellulo structural studies of enzyme filaments, summarizing the insights they provide into filament organization and cellular assembly when available. Together, these findings highlight enzyme filamentation as a common mode of macromolecular organization with consequences for structure, assembly, and function in diverse biological contexts.

42973246.resumo: Doc2s modulate neurotransmitter release through interactions with Munc13-1, SNAREs, lipids, and Ca2+, which involve the Doc2 C2 domains and Munc13-interacting domain (MID). However, it is unclear how these interactions are coupled, how Doc2s bind to Munc13-1, and how they bind to the SNAREs. Here we determined the cryo-electron microscopy structure of a Doc2B-Munc13-1 complex aided by an AI-designed Munc13-1 binder, revealing how Doc2B MID binds to a Munc13-1 hydrophobic pocket essential for opening syntaxin-1 and explaining why Doc2B inhibits SNARE assembly. NMR and fluorescence spectroscopy show that Doc2B MID binds lipids and that MID-lipid and MID-Munc13-1 interactions are mutually exclusive, suggesting that membrane binding helps release the inhibition of Munc13-1. NMR shows that Doc2B binds to the SNARE complex via two helices of C2B. Based on these results and liposome fusion assays, we propose a working model whereby: 1. Doc2B MID-Munc13-1 interactions facilitate synergistic binding of both proteins to the plasma membrane, with the MID inhibiting Munc13-1. 2. Membrane binding facilitates MID-lipid interactions that transiently relieve the inhibition of Munc13-1, allowing SNARE complex assembly. 3. Doc2B binding to the SNARE complex inhibits neurotransmitter release but generates a primed state that mediates neurotransmitter release by an as-yet-unknown mechanism.

42976709.resumo: Light pollution affects about one quarter of the Earth's land surface and is rapidly growing in both extent and intensity with accelerated global urbanization. Artificial light at night (ALAN) constitutes the major source of light pollution and poses significant challenges to the health of many organisms, including pollinators. However, whether and how ALAN exposure affects bumblebees' physiology remain unexplored. Our study aims to preliminarily investigate the effects of ALAN exposure on bumblebees and hypothesizes that it may cause physiological damage to gynes. As we expected, ALAN exposure causes precocious death in gynes. Extended light exposure leads to sleep loss and dysfunctional cognitive performance in gynes. In addition, light pollution also disrupts the nutritional homeostasis in gynes. Transcriptomic analysis revealed altered expression of genes associated with sleep, cognition, and nutrient metabolism, suggesting that ALAN exposure may disrupt gut-brain communication in gynes. Furthermore, systemic accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) is detected in ALAN-exposed gynes due to down-regulation of genes in the glutathione metabolic pathway. Importantly, both oral supplementation with antioxidants and dark recovery effectively suppress excessive ROS production and reverse the detrimental effects after ALAN exposure to gynes. Our study provides evidence of the detrimental effects of light pollution on gynes for the first time and reveals the pivotal role of oxidative stress in mediating light-induced sleep loss, cognitive impairment, and nutrient homeostasis disruption of bumblebees. This further implicates light pollution as a potential contributor to bumblebees' decline.

42974913.resumo: Insect olfaction is facilitated by a heterotetrameric odorant receptor-odorant receptor co-receptor (OR-Orco) complex. However, extensive sequence divergence and lineage-specific expansion have complicated large-scale comparisons of OR repertoires across insects. Here, we integrated sequence similarity, structural similarity, and molecular docking to analyze ORs from 115 insect species. OR repertoire size was associated with adult diet, larval diet, and habitat, but not with circadian rhythm. We developed a 'trunk-branch' network framework to classify ORs according to sequence and structural similarity and used large-scale molecular docking to derive comparative docking profiles. Despite marked differences in sequence- and structural-community composition, almost all sampled orders contained ORs assigned to all six docking-profile communities. Holometabolous insects showed higher OR sequence-community diversity than non-holometabolous insects, and docking-profile composition differed between extant lineages whose order-level origins predate or postdate the end-Permian mass extinction. Most notably, we identified a highly conserved extracellular β-sheet in Orco that restricts ligand access to the binding pocket and may contribute to its reduced capacity to bind natural odorants. The emergence of Orco represents a key evolutionary transition from homomeric receptors to heteromeric OR-Orco complexes, and our results suggest that this transition may have been accompanied by pronounced specialization of the extracellular domain and binding pocket. Together, these analyses provide a class-wide framework for comparing insect OR diversity and generate testable hypotheses for future experimental and evolutionary studies.

42980460.resumo: Plant-delivered Cry proteins effectively control lepidopteran pests, but how midgut injury develops into systemic metabolic and developmental dysfunction remains unclear. Here, fourth instar Hyphantria cunea larvae were fed wild-type (WT), pair-fed wild-type (PF-WT), or Cry1Ac-transgenic Populus × xiaohei leaves. Cry1Ac-transgenic leaf feeding impaired nutrient utilization, growth, survival, and development, disrupted the chitin-associated midgut interface, and reduced α-amylase and lipase activities. Metabolites altered relative to both controls were enriched in glycolysis/gluconeogenesis, pyruvate metabolism, the tricarboxylic acid cycle, and starch and sucrose metabolism. These changes were accompanied by reduced glycolytic activity, ATP content, and adenylate energy charge, increased AMPKα phosphorylation, reduced S6K and 4E-BP phosphorylation, and altered 20E biosynthesis, signaling, and chitin synthesis. Exogenous 20E partially restored molting-related gene expression, epidermal chitin, molting success, and developmental timing, but not feeding or growth. These findings support a proposed digestive-metabolic-endocrine model associated with Cry1Ac-induced molting impairment.

42970597.resumo: The global expansion of mosquito vectors is increasing human exposure to arboviruses, highlighting the need for rapid and practical approaches to assess vector competence. Standard artificial laboratory infection methods rely on infectious blood meals or intrathoracic inoculation, both of which can be resource-intensive and limit the capacity to conduct timely experiments, particularly in high-containment facilities. We developed an infection via sugar meal (IVSM) technique to determine whether mosquitoes can acquire and transmit arboviruses by ingesting virus-spiked sucrose. Using IVSM, we tested the vector competence of Aedes albopictus and Culex quinquefasciatus for West Nile virus (WNV), Mayaro virus (MAYV), and Zika virus (ZIKV) following 1-hour or 24-hour exposures. Viral RNA copy numbers were quantified in the body, legs/wings, and saliva at 7 and 10 days post-infection. Both species supported WNV infection and dissemination, with the virus detected in saliva. Aedes albopictus exhibited high MAYV infection and dissemination rates, whereas Cx. quinquefasciatus was largely refractory. ZIKV infection and dissemination were limited in both species and did not progress to saliva. High feeding success, low vector mortality, and reproducible outcomes across trials demonstrate that IVSM is an accessible and practical alternative to blood-based infection models and provides a framework for investigating vector competence under conditions that utilize natural feeding behavior.

42979312.resumo: Chikungunya fever, caused by the mosquito-borne chikungunya virus (CHIKV), poses a significant global health burden, with an estimated 16.9 million infections annually. Although CHIKV infection induces neutralizing antibody responses, data on their long-term persistence remain limited. In July 2017, an imported outbreak caused by the CHIKV East/Central/South African genotype occurred in Zhejiang Province, China. To assess the longevity of neutralizing antibodies, we conducted a cross-sectional follow-up study in August 2025, approximately eight years after infection. Two laboratory-confirmed patients from the outbreak were enrolled, and serum samples were collected. Serum neutralizing antibodies were measured using both pseudovirus and authentic CHIKV neutralization assays. Remarkably robust and sustained responses were observed in both patients. The pseudovirus neutralization titers were 225,677 and 134,460, respectively, and authentic virus neutralization titers were 9,133 and 4,951, respectively-which substantially exceeded the established protective threshold of 150. As no subsequent CHIKV outbreaks were documented in this non-endemic region, these high neutralizing antibody titers indicate that durable immunity may be derived from a single infection rather than repeated boosting. These findings suggest that natural CHIKV infection can elicit neutralizing antibodies that persist at high levels for at least eight years, providing evidence to inform the development of vaccines and vaccination strategies.

42972442.resumo:
The increasing incidence of dengue in Europe, combined with the spread of invasive mosquito species, raises concerns about the emergence of new vectors. Aedes koreicus, an invasive mosquito rapidly expanding in several European countries, has shown competence for some arboviruses, but its role in dengue virus transmission remains unknown. This study aimed to assess, for the first time, the vector competence of an Italian population of Ae. koreicus for dengue virus serotype 1 (DENV-1).
Laboratory-reared Ae. koreicus females originating from northeastern Italy were orally infected with DENV-1 via an artificial blood meal. Mosquitoes were maintained at 26 ± 1 °C and analysed at 7, 14, 21 and 28 days post-infection (dpi). Infection, dissemination and transmission were evaluated by RT-qPCR and droplet digital PCR, while the presence of infectious virus in saliva was confirmed by virus isolation in Vero E6 cells.
Aedes koreicus was susceptible to DENV-1 infection, with infection rates ranging from 30 to 60% across time points. Viral dissemination to legs and wings was detected from 14 dpi onwards, reaching 100% at 21 and 28 dpi. DENV-1 RNA was detected in saliva at 28 days post-infection (dpi), indicating a relatively long extrinsic incubation period. Overall transmission rate and efficiency were 33.3% and 20%, respectively, at later time points. Infectious virus was successfully isolated from saliva samples confirming transmission capability.
Aedes koreicus was shown to be susceptible to DENV-1 infection and capable of transmitting the virus, although with low efficiency and a long extrinsic incubation period. Despite these limitations, its increasing abundance, longevity and capacity to feed on humans suggest that it may act as a potential dengue vector under favourable conditions. These findings highlight the need to include Ae. koreicus in entomological surveillance and risk assessments for dengue transmission in Europe.

42986483.resumo: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is increasingly recognized as a multicellular neuroimmune disorder in which proteostatic failure, metabolic dysfunction, and sustained glial activation interact to accelerate synaptic loss. This narrative review examines endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress in astrocytes as a mechanistic link among the unfolded protein response (UPR), neuroinflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and neurodegeneration. The three canonical UPR branches, mediated by protein kinase R-like ER kinase (PERK), inositol-requiring enzyme 1 (IRE1), and activating transcription factor 6 (ATF6), initially reduce protein-folding burden and reinforce ER quality control. When stress persists and adaptive capacity becomes insufficient, sustained PERK and IRE1 signaling may favor apoptosis, inflammatory transcriptional programs, cytokine production, calcium dyshomeostasis, and oxidative injury, whereas ATF6 remains predominantly associated with proteostatic reinforcement in a context-dependent manner. In astrocytes, persistent UPR activation may impair neuronal metabolic support, synaptogenic signaling, and astrocytic contributions to neurovascular homeostasis while promoting complement component 3 (C3) expression and bidirectional inflammatory crosstalk with microglia. ER-mitochondria contact sites further integrate calcium transfer, reactive oxygen species generation, bioenergetic failure, and intrinsic apoptotic signaling. Experimental evidence therefore supports a self-reinforcing neuroglial circuit in which astrocytic ER stress is proposed to function as an amplifier rather than merely a consequence of AD pathology. Therapeutic strategies targeting UPR signaling, chemical chaperones, extracellular vesicles, gene modulation, and cell-selective delivery systems remain under investigation, and their translation will require temporally controlled, cell-type-specific, and safety-conscious modulation of stress responses.

42982721.resumo: Trained immunity describes the capacity of innate immune cells to develop memory-like responses following a prior challenge. Early studies focused on myeloid cells and bone marrow progenitors. Extension of this concept to mucosal tissues, however, presents a more complex picture. These barrier sites harbor diverse, long-lived immune populations that interact with structural cells and neuronal circuits to actively shape immune responses. Emerging evidence suggests that memory-like programs extend beyond immune cells to include epithelial, stromal, and neuronal compartments. We propose that trained immunity in mucosal surfaces is distributed across the tissue ecosystem, encompassing progenitors, tissue-resident populations, and the tissue niche. This expanded framework redefines innate immune memory and has important implications for infections and chronic inflammatory diseases.

42981990.resumo:
Phthalates are ubiquitous environmental contaminants, yet their relevance to advanced cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome remains unclear. We examined the associations between urinary phthalate metabolites and advanced CKM syndrome, and explored the potential mechanisms linking di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP)-related exposure to macrophage inflammatory-glycolytic activation.
We analyzed 4236 adults from seven cycles (2005-2018) of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). A total of ten urinary phthalate metabolites were quantified, and advanced CKM syndrome was defined as CKM stages 3-4 using an NHANES-adapted American Heart Association framework. Survey-weighted logistic regression, restricted cubic splines, and weighted quantile sum (WQS) regression were used to assess single-metabolite, dose-response, and mixture associations. Mono(2-ethyl-5-carboxypentyl) phthalate (MECPP) was further evaluated using network toxicology, molecular docking, Mendelian randomization, single-cell RNA sequencing, and macrophage reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR).
Among 4236 participants, 648 had advanced CKM syndrome. In fully adjusted models, oxidative DEHP metabolites were positively associated with advanced CKM syndrome. Compared with the lowest quartile, the highest quartile was associated with higher odds for mono(2-ethyl-5-oxohexyl) phthalate (MEOHP; odds ratio [OR], 1.64; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.12-2.42), mono(2-ethyl-5-hydroxyhexyl) phthalate (MEHHP; OR, 1.60; 95% CI, 1.05-2.42), and MECPP (OR, 1.84; 95% CI, 1.26-2.68), with significant trends. Restricted cubic spline analyses suggested non-linear associations. WQS regression indicated a positive mixture association, with MECPP receiving the highest weight. Network toxicology identified 33 overlapping genes enriched in pathways related to the renin-angiotensin system, insulin resistance, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor signaling, and diabetic cardiomyopathy. Among the candidate hub genes, tumor necrosis factor (TNF) and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARG) were further examined using molecular docking and Mendelian randomization. Single-cell analyses of public mouse heart and kidney datasets localized Tnf mainly to macrophages and Pparg to cardiac endothelial cells and renal monocytes. In RAW 264.7 macrophages, MECPP potentiated palmitic acid-induced expression of inflammatory and glycolysis-related genes.
Urinary oxidative DEHP metabolites, particularly MECPP, were positively associated with advanced CKM syndrome in US adults. These findings support MECPP as a potential biomarker of DEHP-related exposure and generate mechanistic hypotheses involving macrophage-centered inflammatory and glycolytic transcriptional activation. Prospective and experimental studies are warranted to clarify causality and to determine whether DEHP-related exposure contributes to the development and progression of CKM syndrome.

42977037.resumo: Chronic low-grade inflammation (inflammaging) is a central feature of aging, yet its magnitude and trajectory vary substantially among individuals and tissues. This variability is not fully explained by chronological age or cumulative inflammatory exposure. We therefore examine inflammaging through a spatiotemporal framework focused on how inflammatory responses are initiated, contained, resolved, and distributed across tissues. The framework integrates established mechanisms-including defective resolution, epigenetic drift, cellular senescence and the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), cytosolic DNA sensing, inflammasome activation, cytokine dysregulation, and loss of immunometabolic flexibility. We use the term spatiotemporal decoupling to describe the observable divergence between chronological age and inflammatory state across time, tissues, and individuals. The term does not denote a newly discovered molecular pathway; its value lies in organizing existing evidence around failures of regulatory closure and in generating testable predictions about inflammatory persistence and tissue heterogeneity. This perspective suggests that systemic inflammatory markers alone are unlikely to identify the mechanism sustaining inflammation in a given patient or tissue. Therapeutic strategies should therefore be matched to the dominant process and disease context, with attention to tissue delivery, host defense, repair, and other consequences of pathway inhibition. Candidate approaches include restoration of resolution, modulation of senescent-cell burden or SASP, selective control of innate immune sensing and cytokine signaling, and improvement of metabolic flexibility. Overall, the review distinguishes established components of inflammaging from their proposed integration in a spatiotemporal model and identifies the evidence needed to test its translational relevance.

42975958.resumo: Children and adults living with obesity have more severe influenza A virus (IAV) infection, but the underlying mechanisms are unclear. Natural killer (NK) cells play a key role in the innate immune responses to IAV and clearance of IAV-infected cells. 'Trained immunity' of NK cells (and other innate immune cells) refers to an initial stimulus (i.e. obesity) inducing metabolic and epigenetic changes that make these cells hyperinflammatory upon restimulation (i.e. with IAV). Here, we tested whether obesity in children induces trained immunity in NK cells. We have show that NK cells from children with obesity have a hyperinflammatory 'trained' phenotype, with increased expression of activation markers TLR2, CCR2, TLR4, HLA-DR and CD11b compared to children without obesity. Furthermore, we have demonstrate that NK cells from children with obesity have a heightened ex vivo IFN-γ response to stimulation with IAV (A/Auckland/4/2009, H1N1 and HKx31, H3N2) and epigenetic changes consistent trained immunity. A decrease in BMI z-score following weight-management was not associated with a reduction in the IFN-γ response, suggesting that weight loss is not sufficient to normalise NK cell function. Better understanding of obesity-related immune modulation is critical for development of new therapeutic strategies and improving outcomes in future IAV pandemics.

42975756.resumo: Low-dose interleukin-2 (LD-IL-2) is being developed as an immune-regulatory therapy across rheumatic and autoimmune diseases, but its biology cannot be reduced to regulatory T-cell (Treg) expansion. IL-2 responses are determined by dose and exposure, receptor abundance and binding kinetics, activation state, tissue distribution, and the balance among JAK-STAT5, PI3K-AKT-mTOR, and RAS-MAPK signaling. CD25-high Tregs have a competitive advantage at low concentrations, yet activated conventional T cells, CD8 + T cells, natural killer cells, follicular T-cell subsets, B-cell compartments, and tissue-resident populations may also be modulated directly or indirectly. We therefore synthesize the field through a cross-disease framework linking receptor pharmacology, signaling thresholds, Treg heterogeneity, epigenetic and metabolic fitness, receptor trafficking, and tissue microenvironments to pharmacodynamic, clinical, and durable responses. Disease-specific evidence is critically compared rather than interpreted as a uniform IL-2-deficiency syndrome: systemic lupus erythematosus combines T-cell IL-2 deficiency with Tfh-B-cell and age-associated B-cell pathology; inflammatory arthritis is constrained by synovial cytokine consumption and tissue access; systemic sclerosis by vascular-fibrotic remodeling; inflammatory myopathy by muscle, skin, lung, and microbiome contexts; and neurological autoimmunity by blood-brain-barrier penetration and compartmentalized inflammation. Randomized evidence supports biological activity and preliminary efficacy in selected settings, whereas many indications remain supported by small, uncontrolled studies. Native LD-IL-2 and engineered agonists also require separate evaluation because altered affinity and half-life can change cellular selectivity, immunogenicity, biodistribution, and the risk of chronic receptor overstimulation. We conclude that development should prioritize disease-specific dose-exposure relationships, functional and tissue-resolved biomarkers, rigorous clinical endpoints, and long-term surveillance. This framework positions IL-2 therapy as context-dependent network modulation rather than universal restoration of immune tolerance.

Thus, our data highlight that AMs acquire neutrophil enzymes as an integral component of innate immune adaptation.

42980183.resumo:
Creeping fat (CrF) in Crohn's disease (CD) is a metabolically active perilesional adipose tissue involved in intestinal inflammation. Whether biological therapies modify its browning-associated phenotype remains largely unexplored. We investigated whether anti-TNF treatment is associated with changes in browning-, mitochondrial biogenesis- and immune-related pathways in CrF and whether similar molecular changes occur following ex vivo infliximab exposure.
Two independent human cohorts were analysed. (1) Observational cohort: CrF biopsies from anti-TNF-treated and anti-TNF-naïve CD patients (n = 14 and n = 19, respectively) were analysed for metabolic and inflammatory gene and protein expression. AdMSCs and mature CrF-derived adipocytes were isolated, and UCP1 protein abundance was assessed by immunohistochemistry and western blotting. (2) Ex vivo cohort: Paired CrF explants from anti-TNF-naïve patients with CD undergoing surgery were cultured with or without infliximab (5 mg/kg-equivalent, 24 h) and analysed by RT-qPCR and immunohistochemistry.
Anti-TNF-treated patients showed higher UCP1 expression in CrF at mRNA and protein levels. CrF-derived mature adipocytes from treated patients exhibited increased expression of browning-/thermogenesis- and mitochondrial biogenesis-associated genes, together with reduced selected pro-inflammatory markers. AdMSCs also showed exploratory differences in their conditioned-medium protein profile, although no protein remained significant after FDR correction. Ex vivo infliximab exposure was associated with changes in selected browning-, mitochondrial biogenesis- and immune-related markers.
Together, the observational and ex vivo findings identify CrF as an anti-TNF-responsive immunometabolic compartment in CD, characterised by coordinated browning-, mitochondrial biogenesis- and immune-related molecular changes. Functional studies are needed to establish the metabolic significance of these changes.

42969658.titulo: Deciphering Host Genomic Pathway Landscapes in Severe COVID-19 by Exome Sequencing of a Large Admixed Brazilian Cohort.
42969658.autores: Zetum ASS, Silva DRCD, Ventorim VDP, Mion FA, Passarela FDS, Brasil P, Campos TL, Acioli-Santos B, Oliveira FRDS, Trabach RSDR, Altoé LSC, Meira DD, Louro ID

resumo_blocos.racional: A heterogeneidade clínica observada em infecções virais graves permanece insuficientemente explicada apenas por fatores de risco demográficos ou comorbidades clássicas, existindo uma lacuna substancial sobre a contribuição de assinaturas genômicas complexas em populações miscigenadas altamente sub-representadas em biobancos globais. A premissa analítica tradicional baseada estritamente em estudos de associação genômica ampla (GWAS) falha frequentemente em capturar efeitos poligênicos e redes biológicas interconectadas mediados por variantes de frequência alélica intermediária e rara. Diante dessa limitação, os autores formularam a hipótese de que a susceptibilidade ao fenótipo hiperinflamatório e à gravidade clínica da COVID-19 em uma coorte brasileira decorre da disrupção coordenada de eixos biológicos integrados — nomeadamente homeostase mitocondrial, resposta de complemento e estabilidade estrutural de membranas epiteliais/endoteliais.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: O estudo conduziu o sequenciamento completo do exoma (WES) a partir do DNA genômico purificado de leucócitos de sangue periférico de uma coorte de 325 pacientes brasileiros com COVID-19 estratificados clinicamente em casos graves (necessidade de ventilação mecânica/suporte intensivo) e não graves. O pipeline bioinformático utilizou alinhamento ao genoma de referência GRCh38 via BWA-MEM, recalibração de bases e chamada de variantes de nucleotídeo único (SNVs) e indels pelo GATK HaplotypeCaller. Para a priorização genômica de variantes raras e comuns associadas à severidade clínica, foi empregado um algoritmo de aprendizado de máquina supervisionado baseado em Support Vector Machine com Eliminação Recursiva de Características (SVM-RFE) acoplado a valores de SHAP (Shapley Additive Explanations). As variantes preditivas foram submetidas a modelos de regressão logística multivariada corrigidos para idade, sexo biológico, principais componentes (PCs) de ancestralidade genética e comorbidades clínicas, aplicando-se correção de taxa de falsa descoberta (FDR de Benjamini-Hochberg < 0,05) e anotação funcional com CADD e banco GTEx.
resumo_blocos.resultados: O modelo preditivo baseado em SVM-RFE combinado com SHAP selecionou com alta acurácia discriminativa (área sob a curva ROC [AUC] = 0,94) um painel restrito de 25 variantes genômicas capazes de segregar com precisão indivíduos graves de não graves. As análises de regressão logística ajustadas confirmaram associações estatisticamente robustas (FDR < 0,05) em loci funcionais relevantes, destacando polimorfismos e variantes deletérias nos genes MUC16, SLC4A2, LAPS1, ARRDC2 e CCSER1. A anotação fenotípica e funcional (CADD e GTEx) revelou enriquecimento estatístico significativo em vias de integridade estrutural epitelial/mucosa, bioenergética mitocondrial, sinalização imune de complemento e tráfego neural. Os dados consolidam a noção de que a progressão para quadros críticos é governada por uma arquitetura genômica em nível de vias fisiológicas integradas, influenciando diretamente a suscetibilidade a tempestades de citocinas e falência multiorgânica.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado ao programa 'Malária Cerebral & Neuroinflamação' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Embora centrado na patologia induzida por SARS-CoV-2, a identificação de eixos genômicos ligados à integridade de barreiras teciduais, bioenergética mitocondrial e sinalização neuroimune ressoa diretamente com as investigações de disfunção endotelial do LUCHM no modelo de malária cerebral murina (PbA em C57BL/6J). O comprometimento da homeostase iônica e de transportadores de membrana (como SLC4A2 e reguladores de tráfego vesicular como ARRDC2) converge com nossos estudos sobre a perda de junções de oclusão (claudina-5 e ocludina) e edema vasogênico dependente de influxo eletrolítico e dano mitocondrial. Além disso, a modulação de cascatas inflamatórias e do complemento identificadas na coorte oferece pistas moleculares sobre alvos homólogos em células endoteliais e microgliais sob estresse inflamatório agudo, permitindo contrastar determinantes intrínsecos de suscetibilidade a colapso de barreira hematoencefálica.
